text:
support_jane: FYI we got a priority escalation from AcmeCorp (CS-9042). After the rollout last night their markdown outputs have extra fence delimiters and stray dashes. Repro example they sent below.

cs_lead_amy: tagging eng for triage @eng-miguel @eng-ash :exclamation:

support_jane: Request details from customer:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  model: redwood-llama-13b@v2.3.1,
  prompt: '```python\nprint(\'hello\')\n```',
  stop_sequences: ["```", "---"],
  request_id: r-0a1b2c3d
}
```
Response they get:
```
```python
print('hello')
``````
---
```
(note the extra ``` and a leading --- after the fence)

eng_miguel: thanks. can you paste the full response headers and route id? also what percent rollout did we do and when?

tom_custrep: customer included route: /v1/generate?route=default-eu and headers x-route-id: eu-001, no errors in headers. They noticed it started after the 22:00 UTC deploy.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2025-12-12T22:00:00Z completed to 100% - commit abcdef0123

prod_liz: confirmed, rollout finished at 22:00 UTC. Canary was earlier at 20:10 with 10% traffic.

eng_ash: initial suspicion: tokenizer edge-case with stop sequence matching when stop seqs overlap with fenced code markers. We changed a tokenization postprocess in v2.3.1 to speed up continuous batching; could affect decoded-boundary matching.

eng_miguel: repro attempt: running locally with model redwood-llama-13b@v2.3.1 and the same stop list. I can reproduce the extra backticks in ~1/30 responses when prompt ends with a fence. Looks like we match stop sequences on token boundaries instead of the decoded string, so when a fence is split across two tokens we don't trim correctly and the generator emits the leftover literal tokens.

eng_ash: thanks. can you attach a small repro script we can run in CI? Also any latency or API errors reported by customer?

support_jane: no API errors, just content quality. Customer says some outputs also had stray hyphen lines inserted between blocks. Example above shows --- added.

eng_miguel: I'll open an incident and start a hotfix branch. Plan: make stop-sequence matching operate on utf-8 decoded text post-detokenization and add targeted unit tests for fence and hyphen sequences. Patch ETA ~2 hours. If customer wants immediate action we can consider rollback to commit before abcdef0123.

cs_lead_amy: Tom, does AcmeCorp want rollback or to wait for hotfix?

tom_custrep: Customer prefers rollback to minimize user impact. They're blocking release notes until this is resolved.

eng_ash: rollback would reintroduce older batching perf. Can we do a partial rollback by pinning that route to previous model variant for AcmeCorp only? We can create a route override for eu-001.

eng_miguel: I can apply a route-level pin to previous model version v2.3.0 for eu-001. That will take ~15 mins plus validation. Meanwhile I'll push the hotfix branch and run unit tests.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2025-982 created by eng_miguel for markdown delimiter regression.

support_jane: customer updated: they want immediate mitigation, please pin their route and let us know once done.

eng_miguel: pinned eu-001 to redwood-llama-13b@v2.3.0 and confirmed responses back to expected behavior when running the same repro prompt. Route override applied at 23:08 UTC.

tom_custrep: customer confirms pins fixed their issue in staging. They request ETA for full fix.

eng_ash: hotfix merged to canary at 23:20 UTC; tests pass. I'll coordinate a small canary rollout and monitor for fence/hyphen regressions, then promote to prod. ETA full rollout 02:30 UTC if no regressions.

cs_lead_amy: thanks team. followups: add new unit tests for fence overlaps, add an e2e test against a set of stop sequences customers commonly use, and update the release notes with mitigation steps.

support_jane: workaround for other customers in the meantime: suggest removing overlapping stop seqs (avoid using exact fence as stop) or post-process to strip duplicate leading fences. Documenting in the support KB now.

eng_miguel: will follow up with PR link and postmortem once incident is closed.
